content:
maria: Heads-up — raw billing events storage cost spiked 3x last quarter. I want to kick off a short design thread: compacting historical per-request token rows into cheaper audit envelopes while keeping full auditability. thoughts? :chart_with_upwards_trend:

oliver: Curious — are you proposing deletions of raw events or just compressing into a canonical envelope? legal might push back on deletions for audits.

maria: Not deleting. Proposal sketch: keep last 90 days raw for realtime billing + dispute handling. Older than 90d we compact into per-tenant, per-day envelopes with provenance pointers and cryptographic checksums. Uncompacted raw can be reclaimed.

josh: Two quick concerns: backfills + reprocess. If we transform old raw into a compact envelope, any downstream re-run (e.g., new price adjustments) needs ability to reconstruct token-level shape. Can your envelopes deterministically replay?

maria: Yes, goal is deterministic replay. Envelopes will include: aggregate counters, a small set of representative samples (for QA/regression), and an integrity proof that allows checking compaction correctness. Not planning to keep every token, but enough to prove the aggregated numbers.

sehaj: Suggestion: use rolling Merkle roots anchored to an append-only ledger table. Envelope contains merkle_root + compacted deltas + sample_ids. If we ever need a token-level audit, we rehydrate from external cold storage using sample IDs + provenance metadata.

infra-bot: (deploy) scheduled job: compact-old-events v1.2 will run in staging tomorrow 02:00 UTC.

oliver: How long to rehydrate? If a customer escalates a dispute we need SLA on turnaround. Legal wants 30-day response SLA for certain enterprise tiers. Rehydration from blob store could be hours if we need to assemble many shards.

maria: We can tier rehydration SLA by plan: enterprise = 6h, standard = 24h, free = best-effort. For urgent legal holds we can pin tenant raw copy in cold-warm storage (higher $).

josh: Another thought: instead of per-day envelopes, what about semantic windows keyed by model+route so compaction respects billing granularity? e.g., same-day but split by model family to avoid mixing pricing regimes.

maria: Agreed. Envelope key = tenant_id | bill_date | model_family | price_version. That reduces re-aggregation ambiguity when pricing changes.

sehaj: Quick schema idea (rough):
```
{
  "envelope_version": "1",
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "bill_date": "2026-02-10",
  "model_family": "gptx-8k",
  "price_version": "pv-2026-01",
  "aggregates": {"tokens_input": 123456, "tokens_output": 98765, "requests": 4321},
  "sample_ids": ["obj://raw/2026/02/10/slot-1.gz", "obj://raw/2026/02/10/slot-42.gz"],
  "merkle_root": "sha256:...",
  "compaction_proof": "b64sig..."
}
```

qa-anna: For QA and billing regression we rely on prompt/response samples. The sample_ids approach looks good. We should keep deterministic sampling seed so tests are reproducible.

maria: Good call. We'll embed seed + sampling-window in envelope metadata.

oliver: Cost model? What does compacting at 90d save vs 180d? Need a rough estimate to justify work.

maria: Back-of-envelope: current raw retention (365d) costs $X/month. Moving to 90d raw + 275d compacted reduces object storage by ~60% and query/egress costs by ~70%. I'll share exact numbers in a follow-up note.

josh: One operational risk — consistent compaction ordering. If two compaction workers touch overlapping time ranges we could double-count or lose provenance. Need an idempotent compactor with partition-level locks (or single-writer for a partition).

sehaj: We already have a partition-lease service used by ingestion. Reuse it: compactor acquires lease for (tenant, bill_date, model_family) for the run. Writes envelope atomically and emits finalization event to a compacted-changefeed.

maria: That fits. We'll also emit a tombstone pointer for replaced raw segments and a reversible mapping in case of legal holds.

oliver: One more: metrics & alerting. Add a 'compaction-coverage' metric per-tenant + anomalies if envelope aggregates diverge from incremental rollups by >0.5%.

maria: Ack. Plan next steps: (1) prototype envelope writer + Merkle root library, (2) small staging compaction run for low-volume tenants, (3) cost/latency analysis and backfill playbook, (4) RFC doc with SLA tiers + legal check. Volunteers? :raised_hands:

josh: I can help with prototype + proto tests.

sehaj: I'll own merkle/crypto + lease integration.

oliver: I'll coordinate legal/enterprise SLA + ops runbook.

qa-anna: QA + sampling determinism tests from me.

maria: Thanks — I'll open an RFC PR with the envelope schema and initial cost numbers tomorrow.

infra-bot: (reminder) create rfc/compaction-envelopes in the repo: https://git.redwood/c/infra/rfcs/compaction-envelopes
